body.en: A quadratic equation with a negative discriminant has no real solutions — the parabola never crosses the \( x \)-axis. Complex numbers resolve this: by defining a number whose square is \( -1 \), every quadratic (in fact, every polynomial) gets exactly as many roots as its degree.

label.en: ● Definition 1.1 — The imaginary unit and complex numbers

body.en: The imaginary unit \( i \) is defined by \( i^2=-1 \). A complex number \( z=a+bi \) pairs a real part \( a \) with an imaginary part \( b \) (both real numbers). Two complex numbers are equal exactly when their real parts match and their imaginary parts match.

Complex numbers add, subtract, and multiply using ordinary algebra, replacing \( i^2 \) with \( -1 \) wherever it appears. For \( z_1=a+bi \), \( z_2=c+di \):

\[ z_1\pm z_2=(a\pm c)+(b\pm d)i, \qquad z_1z_2=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i. \]

The most common way a Level 2 question meets complex numbers is by asking you to solve a quadratic that the discriminant test says has no real roots. The quadratic formula still works — it just hands back a complex answer.

label.en: ▲ Theorem 1.1 — Complex roots of a quadratic

body.en:
For \( ax^2+bx+c=0 \) with real \( a,b,c \) (\( a\neq0 \)) and discriminant \( \Delta=b^2-4ac<0 \), the two roots are the complex conjugate pair

\[ x=-\frac{b}{2a}\pm i\,\frac{\sqrt{4ac-b^2}}{2a}. \]

The quadratic formula gives \( x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} \) regardless of the sign of the discriminant. When \( \Delta=b^2-4ac<0 \), write \( b^2-4ac=-(4ac-b^2) \), where \( 4ac-b^2>0 \) since \( \Delta<0 \). Then

\[ \sqrt{b^2-4ac}=\sqrt{-(4ac-b^2)}=\sqrt{4ac-b^2}\cdot\sqrt{-1}=i\sqrt{4ac-b^2}, \]

using \( i=\sqrt{-1} \) from Definition 1.1. Substituting back:

\[ x=\frac{-b\pm i\sqrt{4ac-b^2}}{2a}=-\frac{b}{2a}\pm i\,\frac{\sqrt{4ac-b^2}}{2a}. \]

The two roots share the same real part \( -\tfrac{b}{2a} \) and have opposite-sign imaginary parts — exactly the definition of a conjugate pair. \( \blacksquare \)

label.en: Worked example 1.B — Solving a quadratic with complex roots

value.en: A conjugate pair \( a\pm bi \) always has equal modulus for both roots
